correctness.rationale: From the displayed hyperbolic Laplacian and separation into degree-m spherical harmonics, the regular radial factor is S_m(t)=1+(m/2)(1−t), satisfying (1−t)[4tS''+4(m+2)S']+4[mS+2tS']=0. The radial mass density t^{m+1}(1−t)^s S_m(t)² gives the exact beta-integral quotient and multiplicity (m+1)². Differentiating log(p_{m+1}/p_m) gives 1/t−1/(S_m S_{m+1})>0, establishing stochastic-order strict decrease. Endpoint asymptotics yield Λ_m~T²(1−T)^{s+2}m^{s+2}T^m/[Γ(s+1)(s+2)(s+5)] versus Euclidean E_m~T²(1−T)^s m^s T^m/Γ(s+1). Threshold inversion m=L/c+(a/c)log L+O(1) and ∑_{m≤M}(m+1)²=M³/3+O(M²) give coefficient 2/c³ of L²log L. Independently checked the radial PDE for m≤14 and rational integral spectra/monotonicity for s=0,...,3, T=1/4,1/2,3/4 and m≤14.

originality.rationale: Blaschke–Engliš–Youssfi provide the precise H-harmonic weighted Bergman spaces, spherical decomposition and radial factor S_m in their primary article, so those foundations and the denominator integral are unequivocally prior art. Their actual full PDF Section 2, Eqs. 2–6, does not formulate the inner-ball concentration operator, strict eigenvalue ordering or Euclidean-vs-H-harmonic counting excess; searches of the PDF found no concentration/Toeplitz/eigenvalues section. The surviving novelty is the spectral comparison and universal logarithmic excess, not the known radial profile.
